title: Void Ending in a Trine to Venus
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Venus, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of her sweetness and her song. Venus governs taste, the text says, and with it beauty and love: poetic meter, songs, dancing, painting, and perfumes fall to her, with places of music and merriment among her locations. She is the Lesser Fortune, and her benevolence fits the works of youths, pleasures, and women. Pearls are her stones, the sweet smells are hers, and her colors are sky blue and gold fading into green.
